# Maskera (maskera.dev)

> Swedish-first, local privacy layer in front of every AI model. maskera finds and masks detected Swedish personal data (names, personnummer, addresses, phone numbers, and more) before text reaches an LLM, an AI agent, a log, or analytics. Everything runs on-device (browser via WebGPU/WASM, browser extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox with Safari coming later, local LLM proxy / MCP server via `@maskera/mcp`, or Node); text and restore maps are not sent away for masking. The packages contain no telemetry. The demo counts anonymous, cookieless page views, never your content. The default setup fetches the model weights and WASM runtime once as static assets (both can be self-hosted), never your content. Redactions are reversible via a restore map that stays with the caller.

Three open-source packages (MIT), two detection layers (rules first):

- `@maskera/mcp` (npm): local-first CLI for AI agents with three modes on top of `maskera`:
  1. `npx -y @maskera/mcp proxy`: harness-agnostic local HTTP reverse proxy on `127.0.0.1:8787` for Anthropic (`/v1/messages`) and OpenAI (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`). Automatically redacts outgoing prompts, history and tool results before they leave the device, restores placeholders transparently in JSON, tool arguments and chunk-split SSE streams, and fails closed (`502`) on error. Point `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787` or `OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1` (or pass `--upstream <url>`).
  2. `npx -y @maskera/mcp --root <dir>`: MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio server (`maskera_read_file`, `maskera_write_file`, `maskera_redact`, `maskera_restore`, `maskera_list_sessions`, `maskera_clear_session`, `maskera_status`). Keeps raw file contents and restore maps strictly inside local process memory.
  3. `npx -y @maskera/mcp guard`: harness-agnostic hook/pipe guard. Reads plain text, `--file <path>`, or Claude Code/Cursor JSON hook envelopes from stdin; exits `2` with label counts only (never raw PII) when PII is found, or outputs redacted text with `--redact`.
- `@maskera/core` (npm): deterministic detectors for structured Swedish PII: personnummer, samordningsnummer, organisationsnummer, phone, email, postnummer, bankgiro, plusgiro, IBAN, cards, IP, URL, plus opt-in context-labeled domestic account and journal identifiers. Format checks and selective checksums reject common look-alikes; personnummer detection deliberately retains real-date values with a mistyped Luhn digit. Zero dependencies, synchronous. Custom patterns join via `regexDetector`.
- `maskera` (npm): everything in core plus the published `maskera-sv-ner` v20, our attested privacy-clean Swedish NER model (KB-BERT fine-tuned and distilled from a 3-seed teacher ensemble to a 43 MB ONNX) that catches free-text names, places, organisations and street addresses, including all-lowercase chat text. Its task-specific training uses 108,400 generated rows and 6,900 disjoint validation rows. On overlap, rules win. The hybrid also enables street address, lägenhetsnummer and context-labeled domestic account/journal identifiers by default; `regnummer` is opt-in. Clinical callers can set `profile: "clinical"` to retain common measurements, doses and care terms.

Quick start (SDK):

```ts
import { createNerRecognizer, redactWithNer } from "maskera"

const recognizer = createNerRecognizer()
const { text, restore } = await redactWithNer(
  "hej jag heter provnamn maskera, personnummer 19900101-2385, och bor i provbyn",
  { recognizer },
)
// "hej jag heter [NAMN_1], personnummer [PERSONNUMMER_1], och bor i [PLATS_1]"
```

Published-v20 release gates (q4; release measured 2026-11-25): curated span F1 99.5% with 0/205 leaks, revised synthetic ADR label-agnostic span F1 100.0% with 0/57 leaks (35/35 ADDRESS precision; 98.2% labeled F1), LinkedIn-style span F1 98.1% with 0/53 leaks, and rare-surname masked recall 96.60%. Historical v18 public-model comparisons remain separately labeled and do not automatically transfer to v20: https://github.com/joelhagvall/maskera/blob/main/docs/BENCHMARKS.md

Current v20 vs models supporting Swedish (121 hand-authored synthetic Swedish texts, 211 PER/LOC/ORG entities, overlap matching): Maskera q4 (43 MB) masked 211/211 with original casing and 211/211 lowercased; KBLab fp32 (496 MB, measured 2026-11-25) masked 205/211 and 187/211; Bards AI EU PII v3 int8 ONNX (309 MB, 24 EU languages incl. Swedish, measured 2026-11-26) masked 181/211 (85.8%) and 119/211 (56.4%). Typed F1 was 88.2% vs 89.4% vs 74.6% original and 87.4% vs 83.2% vs 62.1% lowercased. This is author-coupled directional evidence, not an independent ranking. Machine results: https://github.com/joelhagvall/maskera/blob/main/docs/benchmark-kblab-v20.json and https://github.com/joelhagvall/maskera/blob/main/docs/benchmark-bardsai-v20.json

Full Swedish hybrid pipeline (2026-11-25; 258 synthetic Swedish domain texts, 952 annotated PII strings): Maskera v20 q4 reached 943/952 (99.1%) full hits, with 3 partial leaks and 6 clear-text misses.

Local PII tool comparison on the exact same 258-text Swedish domain corpus (2026-11-26, strict material-character scorer, CPU): Maskera v20 q4 (43 MB, 12.7 ms/text, 334 MB RAM) reached 98.8% (941/952, 11 leaks; 87/87 lowercase Swedish person names); swedish-pii 1.2.0 (5 MB, regex + name lists) reached 88.3% (841/952, 111 leaks; 0/87 lowercase person names); OpenAI Privacy Filter q4 ONNX (945 MB, 40.3 ms/text, 1,232 MB RAM) reached 72.2% (687/952, 265 leaks; 9/87 lowercase person names); Microsoft Presidio 2.2.366 with Swedish spaCy sv_core_news_lg (245 MB) + Swedish ID rules reached 69.0% (657/952, 295 leaks; 58/87 lowercase person names); LogosGuard 2.4.4 reached 63.7% (606/952, 346 leaks). Machine results: https://github.com/joelhagvall/maskera/blob/main/docs/benchmark-swedish-products-v20.json

Deployment boundary: all masking runs locally on the user's device, whether in the open-source npm packages (`maskera`, `@maskera/core`, `@maskera/mcp`), the maskera.dev browser demo, or the Maskera browser extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox (Safari coming later; Free with unlimited rules + 20 AI redactions/month, or Pro at SEK 149/user/month incl. VAT with a 7-day free trial, shared E2EE org protected words and MDM deployment). There is no hosted masking API on offer. The customer portal at app.maskera.dev handles accounts, offline extension licences, and billing. Customer text is not processed there.

## When to use Maskera

Reach for Maskera when all of these hold:

- The text is Swedish (or mixed Swedish/English) and may contain personal data: names, personnummer, samordningsnummer, organisationsnummer, addresses, phone numbers, e-mail, postnummer, bankgiro/plusgiro, IBAN, card numbers, IP addresses.
- The text is about to leave a trust boundary: a prompt to an LLM or AI agent, a local file read by an agent, a log line, analytics, a ticket export, a support transcript, a training or evaluation corpus.
- Masking must happen where the text already is (browser, browser extension, local agent proxy/MCP, Node.js) rather than in a third-party API, and it must be reversible for the caller (restore map) but not for the recipient.

Best-fit jobs: enforced pre-LLM redaction for AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Claude Desktop, OpenCode), pre-LLM redaction in ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Perplexity, Mistral and internal AI sites, HR/recruiting screening, customer support and complaints, healthcare notes (`profile: "clinical"` keeps doses and measurements), legal and municipal case text, log scrubbing, building de-identified test data from real-looking Swedish text.

Not a fit: non-Swedish text (English names work only incidentally), image/PDF OCR (feed Maskera the extracted text), a hosted "send us your text" API (none exists, by design), or guarantees of zero leaks (see the measured leak counts above and the accuracy page).

## How an agent should call it

Pick the right local integration for the user's environment:

1. **Enforced redaction across any agent harness (recommended when the user wants zero-trust redaction of all prompts and tool outputs):**
   - Start `npx -y @maskera/mcp proxy` (binds `127.0.0.1:8787`, supports `--port`, `--upstream <url>`, `--rules-only`, `--profile clinical`, `--custom-term <word>`, `--no-restore`).
   - Configure the agent/SDK base URL:
     - Claude Code / Anthropic SDK: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787`
     - Codex / Cursor / OpenAI SDK: `OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1`
   - Check counts without exposing PII: `GET http://127.0.0.1:8787/_maskera/status`.

2. **MCP stdio server (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, T3 Code):**
   - Add to the client's `mcpServers` config:
     ```json
     {
       "mcpServers": {
         "maskera": {
           "command": "npx",
           "args": ["-y", "@maskera/mcp", "--root", "/path/to/workspace"]
         }
       }
     }
     ```
   - Use `maskera_read_file` to read sensitive local files already redacted, `maskera_write_file` to restore placeholders directly to disk without echoing PII into the LLM context, and `maskera_clear_session` when finished.

3. **Hook / shell guard (Claude Code / Cursor hooks or Unix pipes):**
   - Block prompts or hook JSON containing PII: `npx -y @maskera/mcp guard` (exits `2` on PII with counts only, `0` when clean).
   - Redact a stream locally: `cat file.txt | npx -y @maskera/mcp guard --redact`.

4. **Agent skill (workflow rules for any harness):**
   - Install the skill directly from GitHub (`skills/maskera/SKILL.md`): `npx skills add joelhagvall/maskera`.

5. **In application code (browser or Node):**
   - `npm install maskera @huggingface/transformers` (rules + 43 MB Swedish NER model) or `npm install @maskera/core` (rules only, zero dependencies, synchronous). Use `redact(text)` from core, or `createNerRecognizer()` + `redactWithNer(text, { recognizer })` from `maskera`. Keep `map`, send `text`, call `restore(reply)` on the LLM output.

6. **In web AI chats (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Perplexity, Mistral and opt-in internal AI sites):**
   - Install the local Maskera browser extension (Chrome, Edge, Firefox; Safari coming later) from https://maskera.dev/en/services (Swedish: https://maskera.dev/tjanster; Free with unlimited rules + 20 AI redactions/month, or Pro at SEK 149/user/month incl. VAT with a 7-day free trial, shared E2EE org protected words and MDM support via https://app.maskera.dev).

7. **On this site:**
   - Every page has a Markdown rendering. Send `Accept: text/markdown` to any page URL, or fetch the `.md` sibling directly (`https://maskera.dev/index.md`, `https://maskera.dev/en/developers.md`, `https://maskera.dev/en/about.md`). Unknown paths return HTTP 404 with a Markdown (default), JSON (`Accept: application/json` or `/api/*`) or HTML body that lists these entry points. `maskera.dev/api/*` is not an API: it answers 404 in JSON with the same hints.

## Packages and model

- [@maskera/mcp on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@maskera/mcp): local LLM proxy, MCP stdio server, and hook guard for AI agents
- [maskera on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/maskera): rules + Swedish NER model, core re-exported
- [@maskera/core on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@maskera/core): rules only, zero dependencies
- [maskera-sv-ner on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/joelhagvall/maskera-sv-ner): the 43 MB Swedish NER ONNX model, training details
